text: "The database feels slow" is a symptom, not a diagnosis — CPU-bound, IO-bound, and memory-bound each have a different fix. Scaling compute without asking which resource is exhausted often just makes a query-design problem more expensive to ignore.

High signal_wait_time_ms means queries are ready and waiting for a free core — genuinely CPU-bound. High PAGEIOLATCH waits point to IO-bound — but a missing index forcing full scans wears an IO-bound costume that no storage upgrade fixes.

High RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE waits and falling page life expectancy signal memory pressure — a real shortage, or a query reading far more data than it needs. Every category has the same fork: real shortage, or query problem dressed up as a resource symptom.

That closes Chapter 9 — maintenance, integrity, scoped tuning, Resource Governor, and telling a real bottleneck from a query problem. Chapter 10 automates the routine work with SQL Server Agent, starting with what Agent actually does.
